title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Installing assembly-active, responsive, or catalytic sites on ligands couples the coordination sphere to higher-order function, including solid-state CPL, size-selective rare-earth separation, and exposed 3d–4f catalytic sites.
explanation: Long alkyl chains are said to drive alkyl–alkyl packing that enhances solid-state circularly polarized emission. Carboxyl groups on a macrocycle exploit lanthanide-contraction radius differences to precipitate selected ions. In a porous Co–Gd cluster, methyl-modified iminodiacetic acid improves solubility, 3d ions supply catalysis, 4f ions supply structural support, and displacement of surface solvent exposes sites for visible-light CO2-to-CO reduction.
scope: Functional-ligand design of rare-earth complexes, macrocycles, and 3d–4f coordination clusters.
conditions: Alkyl–alkyl assembly for CPL; macrocyclic carboxylates for size selection; visible light and displaceable coordinated solvent for the Co–Gd CO2 reduction example.
caveats: These are parallel design examples, not one ligand motif that simultaneously delivers CPL, separation, and catalysis.
